note: 60 hand-picked field-emergence and field-marriage events for recall estimation (see FIELD_EMERGENCE_STUDY.md, section 3). Citations were written from memory and have NOT been checked against the sources, except those listed in spotChecks. Treat every citation as a lead until verified. Dates are year intervals [start, end]; null means not established. Negative years are BCE. Event type, field assignment and dates are interpretive and contested; datesNote and confidence say where.

types.birth-by-abstraction: A recurring pattern in one field is made an object of its own
types.birth-by-fusion: A field is created by joining two or more others
types.technique-transfer: A tool from field A settles a question native to field B
types.dictionary-analogy: A systematic correspondence between fields is found, then exploited
types.reification: A field's methods become a theory in their own right
types.import-from-outside: A question or tool enters from outside mathematics (physics, games, engineering...)
types.split: A sub-area stops talking to its parent and becomes its own discipline

dateKeys.conceptual: first object, definition or statement of the new idea
dateKeys.methodological: first tool used on purpose on the target
dateKeys.institutional: named chapter, textbook, journal, chair, department or code

fieldVocabulary.note: internal values match technique-vocabulary.json `fields`; `from` lists fields supplying the idea or tool, `to` lists fields receiving it or hosting the new field

events.name: Archimedes' mechanical method for areas and volumes
events.datesNote: The Method is undated; placed within Archimedes' lifetime.
events.summary: Balancing figures on a lever (centres of gravity) is used to discover area and volume results later proved by exhaustion.
keyWorks: Archimedes, The Method (Ephodos), addressed to Eratosthenes
secondary: T. L. Heath (ed.), The Works of Archimedes, with The Method of Archimedes (Cambridge, 1912)
R. Netz and W. Noel, The Archimedes Codex (2007)

events.name: Algebra as a discipline (al-Khwarizmi)
events.datesNote: Whether this is the birth of algebra or a stage in it is the standard historiographic dispute; Diophantus and Babylonian procedures precede it.
events.summary: Problem-solving with unknowns is organised around a small set of normal-form equations with systematic geometric justification, giving algebra its own objects and rules.
keyWorks: al-Khwarizmi, al-Kitab al-mukhtasar fi hisab al-jabr wa-l-muqabala (c. 820)
Omar Khayyam, Treatise on Demonstration of Problems of Algebra (c. 1070)
secondary: R. Rashed, The Development of Arabic Mathematics: Between Arithmetic and Algebra (1994)
R. Rashed, Al-Khwarizmi: The Beginnings of Algebra (2009)

events.name: Analytic geometry
events.datesNote: Viete's analytic art (1591) and Fermat's isagoge (written c. 1636, printed 1679) run in parallel with Descartes.
events.summary: Curves are identified with equations in two unknowns, so geometric problems become algebraic ones and conversely.
keyWorks: R. Descartes, La Geometrie (1637)
P. de Fermat, Ad locos planos et solidos isagoge (c. 1636; publ. 1679)
secondary: C. B. Boyer, History of Analytic Geometry (1956)
H. J. M. Bos, Redefining Geometrical Exactness: Descartes' Transformation of the Early Modern Concept of Construction (2001)

events.name: The calculus
events.datesNote: Tangent and quadrature methods (Cavalieri, Fermat, Barrow) and infinite series (Mercator, Newton) are unified by the inverse relation; institutional end-point is Euler's Introductio (1748) centring functions.
events.summary: Tangent, quadrature and series techniques are unified into an algorithm with a notation, with the inverse relation between differentiation and integration as its core.
keyWorks: G. W. Leibniz, Nova methodus pro maximis et minimis, Acta Eruditorum (1684)
I. Newton, De analysi per aequationes numero terminorum infinitas (written 1669; publ. 1711)
L. Euler, Introductio in analysin infinitorum (1748)
secondary: C. B. Boyer, The History of the Calculus and Its Conceptual Development (1949)
A. R. Hall, Philosophers at War: The Quarrel between Newton and Leibniz (1980)

events.name: Probability from games of chance
events.datesNote: Analysis enters systematically with Laplace's 1812 treatise.
events.summary: The problem of points and dice questions are solved by counting equally likely cases, then generalised into a calculus of chance and, with Laplace, an analytic one.
keyWorks: Pascal-Fermat correspondence (1654)
C. Huygens, De ratiociniis in ludo aleae (1657)
J. Bernoulli, Ars conjectandi (1713)
P.-S. Laplace, Theorie analytique des probabilites (1812)
secondary: A. Hald, A History of Probability and Statistics and Their Applications before 1750 (1990)
L. Daston, Classical Probability in the Enlightenment (1988)

events.name: Graph theory from the Konigsberg bridges
events.datesNote: Euler's paper is a one-off for a century; Kirchhoff (1847) and Cayley/Sylvester (1870s) give tools; Konig's 1936 textbook is the institutional marker.
events.summary: A puzzle about walks across bridges is stripped to vertices and edges, and a parity condition settles it, an early instance of 'geometry of position'.
keyWorks: L. Euler, Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis, Commentarii Academiae Scientiarum Petropolitanae 8 (1736; publ. 1741)
D. Konig, Theorie der endlichen und unendlichen Graphen (1936)
secondary: N. L. Biggs, E. K. Lloyd and R. J. Wilson, Graph Theory 1736-1936 (1976)

events.name: Analytic number theory
events.datesNote: Euler's product (1737), Dirichlet's characters and L-series (1837), Riemann's explicit connection of primes to zeta zeros (1859), proof of the prime number theorem (1896).
events.summary: Infinite series, complex functions and Fourier-type characters are used to count and locate primes.
keyWorks: L. Euler, Variae observationes circa series infinitas (1737; publ. 1744)
P. G. L. Dirichlet, Beweis des Satzes, dass jede unbegrenzte arithmetische Progression ... unendlich viele Primzahlen enthalt, Abh. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. (1837)
B. Riemann, Uber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grosse, Monatsber. Berlin Akad. (1859)
J. Hadamard, Bull. Soc. Math. France 24 (1896); C. J. de la Vallee Poussin, Ann. Soc. Sci. Bruxelles 20 (1896)
secondary: W. Narkiewicz, The Development of Prime Number Theory (2000)
H. M. Edwards, Riemann's Zeta Function (1974)

events.name: Group theory from the solution of polynomial equations
events.datesNote: Lagrange's resolvents (1770-71), Ruffini/Abel on the quintic, Galois (1831, publ. 1846); abstract definition by Cayley (1854) and Weber (1893); Jordan's Traite (1870), Burnside's text (1897).
events.summary: Permutations of roots, first a tool for solving equations, become an object studied for its own structure and are then axiomatised independently of permutations.
keyWorks: J.-L. Lagrange, Reflexions sur la resolution algebrique des equations, Nouv. Mem. Acad. Berlin (1770-71)
N. H. Abel, J. reine angew. Math. 1 (1826)
E. Galois, Memoire sur les conditions de resolubilite des equations par radicaux (1831; publ. J. Math. Pures Appl. 11, 1846)
A. Cayley, On the theory of groups, as depending on the symbolic equation theta^n = 1, Phil. Mag. 7 (1854)
C. Jordan, Traite des substitutions et des equations algebriques (1870)
H. Weber, Math. Ann. 43 (1893)
secondary: H. Wussing, The Genesis of the Abstract Group Concept (1984; German 1969)
R. Kiernan, The development of Galois theory from Lagrange to Artin, Arch. Hist. Exact Sci. 8 (1971)

events.name: Fourier series: heat flow to analysis
events.datesNote: Fourier's memoir (1807) and book (1822); Dirichlet's convergence theorem (1829) is the first rigorous treatment.
events.summary: The heat equation leads to arbitrary functions represented as trigonometric series, forcing a redefinition of function and integral.
keyWorks: J. Fourier, Theorie analytique de la chaleur (1822)
P. G. L. Dirichlet, Sur la convergence des series trigonometriques, J. reine angew. Math. 4 (1829)
secondary: I. Grattan-Guinness, Joseph Fourier 1768-1830 (1972)
U. Bottazzini, The Higher Calculus: A History of Real and Complex Analysis from Euler to Weierstrass (1986)

events.name: Riemannian geometry and manifolds
events.datesNote: Gauss on intrinsic curvature of surfaces (1827/28), Riemann's lecture (1854, publ. 1868); Christoffel (1869) and Ricci-Levi-Civita (1900) supply the calculus.
events.summary: Intrinsic geometry of surfaces is generalised to n-dimensional spaces with a metric given by a quadratic form, with the question of physical space in view.
keyWorks: C. F. Gauss, Disquisitiones generales circa superficies curvas (1828)
B. Riemann, Uber die Hypothesen, welche der Geometrie zu Grunde liegen (1854; publ. 1868)
secondary: E. Scholz, The concept of manifold, 1850-1950, in I. M. James (ed.), History of Topology (1999)
M. Spivak, A Comprehensive Introduction to Differential Geometry, vol. 2 (1979)

events.name: Ideals and algebraic number theory
events.datesNote: Kummer's ideal numbers (1840s) after failures of unique factorisation in cyclotomic arithmetic; Dedekind's ideals (1871); Hilbert's Zahlbericht (1897).
events.summary: Failure of unique factorisation in rings of integers is repaired by introducing ideal elements, later recast as ideals, which become the central object.
keyWorks: E. E. Kummer, Zur Theorie der complexen Zahlen, J. reine angew. Math. 35 (1847) 319-326 (overview; proofs in the companion Uber die Zerlegung der aus Wurzeln der Einheit gebildeten complexen Zahlen in ihre Primfactoren, same volume, 327-367)
R. Dedekind, Supplement XI to Dirichlet's Vorlesungen uber Zahlentheorie (1871)
D. Hilbert, Die Theorie der algebraischen Zahlkorper (Zahlbericht, 1897)
secondary: H. M. Edwards, The genesis of ideal theory, Arch. Hist. Exact Sci. 23 (1980)
H. M. Edwards, Fermat's Last Theorem: A Genetic Introduction to Algebraic Number Theory (1977)

events.name: Riemann surfaces and geometric function theory
events.datesNote: Riemann's thesis (1851) and Abelian functions paper (1857); Klein (1882) and Weyl's Die Idee der Riemannschen Flache (1913) fix the abstract notion.
events.summary: Multi-valued algebraic functions are replaced by single-valued functions on a covering surface, so topological invariants (genus) govern analytic questions.
keyWorks: B. Riemann, Grundlagen fur eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veranderlichen complexen Grosse (1851)
B. Riemann, Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen, J. reine angew. Math. 54 (1857)
H. Weyl, Die Idee der Riemannschen Flache (1913)
secondary: U. Bottazzini and J. Gray, Hidden Harmony - Geometric Fantasies: The Rise of Complex Function Theory (2013)
F. Klein, Uber Riemanns Theorie der algebraischen Functionen und ihrer Integrale (1882)

events.name: Set theory from trigonometric series
events.datesNote: Uniqueness of trigonometric series leads to derived point sets (1872), then non-denumerability (1874) and transfinite numbers (1883); Beitrage (1895-97).
events.summary: Exceptional sets in a uniqueness theorem for Fourier series are classified by derived sets, leading to cardinality and ordinals as a theory of their own.
keyWorks: G. Cantor, Uber die Ausdehnung eines Satzes aus der Theorie der trigonometrischen Reihen, Math. Ann. 5 (1872)
G. Cantor, Uber eine Eigenschaft des Inbegriffes aller reellen algebraischen Zahlen, J. reine angew. Math. 77 (1874)
G. Cantor, Beitrage zur Begrundung der transfiniten Mengenlehre, Math. Ann. 46 (1895), 49 (1897)
secondary: J. W. Dauben, Georg Cantor: His Mathematics and Philosophy of the Infinite (1979)
M. Hallett, Cantorian Set Theory and Limitation of Size (1984)

events.name: Klein's Erlangen programme: geometry as invariants of a group
events.datesNote: Programmatic text (1872) predates its wide influence; Hawkins argues its immediate effect was modest.
events.summary: Each geometry is characterised by a transformation group and its invariants, giving a dictionary between geometric and algebraic statements and ordering the projective, affine, Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometries.
keyWorks: F. Klein, Vergleichende Betrachtungen uber neuere geometrische Forschungen (Erlangen, 1872)
secondary: T. Hawkins, The Erlanger Programm of Felix Klein: reflections on its place in the history of mathematics, Historia Math. 11 (1984)
G. Birkhoff and M. K. Bennett, Felix Klein and his 'Erlanger Programm', in History and Philosophy of Modern Mathematics (1988)

events.name: Lie theory
events.datesNote: Lie's symmetry method for differential equations; Killing and Cartan classify the simple algebras (1888-1894); Lie-Engel treatise (1888-93).
events.summary: Continuous symmetry groups of differential equations are studied through their infinitesimal generators, leading to a structure theory and classification of Lie algebras.
keyWorks: S. Lie and F. Engel, Theorie der Transformationsgruppen, 3 vols (1888-1893)
W. Killing, Die Zusammensetzung der stetigen endlichen Transformationsgruppen, Math. Ann. 31 (1888) to 36 (1890)
E. Cartan, thesis, Sur la structure des groupes de transformations finis et continus (1894)
secondary: T. Hawkins, Emergence of the Theory of Lie Groups: An Essay in the History of Mathematics 1869-1926 (2000)

events.name: Algebraic topology: Betti numbers to homology groups
events.datesNote: Poincare's Analysis situs and complements (1895-1904); Noether's remark that Betti numbers should be ranks of groups, taken up by Hopf and Mayer c. 1925-1929; Alexandroff-Hopf Topologie I (1935).
events.summary: Numerical invariants (Betti numbers) of manifolds from the study of integrals and differential equations are replaced by groups, so algebra becomes the language of topology.
keyWorks: H. Poincare, Analysis situs, J. Ecole Polytech. 1 (1895)
H. Poincare, Complement a l'Analysis situs, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 13 (1899)
P. Alexandroff and H. Hopf, Topologie I (1935)
secondary: J. Dieudonne, A History of Algebraic and Differential Topology, 1900-1960 (1989)
F. Hirzebruch, Emmy Noether and topology, in M. Teicher (ed.), The Heritage of Emmy Noether (1999)

events.name: Commutative algebra from invariant theory and ideals
events.datesNote: Hilbert's finiteness and Nullstellensatz papers (1890-93); Noether's Idealtheorie (1921); van der Waerden's Moderne Algebra (1930-31).
events.summary: Non-constructive finiteness arguments for invariants and ideals of polynomials replace computation, and rings become the unit of study.
keyWorks: D. Hilbert, Uber die Theorie der algebraischen Formen, Math. Ann. 36 (1890)
D. Hilbert, Uber die vollen Invariantensysteme, Math. Ann. 42 (1893)
E. Noether, Idealtheorie in Ringbereichen, Math. Ann. 83 (1921)
B. L. van der Waerden, Moderne Algebra (1930-31)
secondary: L. Corry, Modern Algebra and the Rise of Mathematical Structures (2nd ed., 2004)

events.name: Functional analysis
events.datesNote: Integral equations (Volterra, Fredholm, Hilbert 1904-10), abstract spaces (Frechet 1906, Riesz), Banach's 1932 monograph.
events.summary: Integral equations and the calculus of variations are treated as linear algebra in infinite-dimensional normed spaces with topological structure.
keyWorks: D. Hilbert, Grundzuge einer allgemeinen Theorie der linearen Integralgleichungen (1912; papers 1904-10)
M. Frechet, Sur quelques points du calcul fonctionnel, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 22 (1906)
F. Riesz, Sur les operations fonctionnelles lineaires, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 149 (1909)
S. Banach, Theorie des operations lineaires (1932)
secondary: J. Dieudonne, History of Functional Analysis (1981)
A. F. Monna, Functional Analysis in Historical Perspective (1973)

events.name: Measure theory meets probability (Kolmogorov)
events.datesNote: Borel (1898), Lebesgue (1901-02), Borel's strong law (1909); Kolmogorov's axioms (1933).
events.summary: Probability is axiomatised as a normalised measure on a sigma-algebra, so limit theorems become statements about integration.
keyWorks: E. Borel, Lecons sur la theorie des fonctions (1898)
H. Lebesgue, Integrale, longueur, aire, Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. 7 (1902)
A. N. Kolmogorov, Grundbegriffe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung (1933)
secondary: T. Hawkins, Lebesgue's Theory of Integration: Its Origins and Development (1970)
G. Shafer and V. Vovk, The sources of Kolmogorov's Grundbegriffe, Statistical Science 21 (2006)

events.name: Group representations enter quantum mechanics
events.product: Representation theory of locally compact groups; harmonic analysis on groups
events.datesNote: Peter-Weyl (1927), Weyl (1928), Wigner (1931); Pontryagin duality (1934) and Weil's integration on groups (1940) extend it.
events.summary: Symmetry groups of atoms and spectra are analysed by decomposing the state space into irreducible representations, which also drives the general theory.
keyWorks: F. Peter and H. Weyl, Die Vollstandigkeit der primitiven Darstellungen einer geschlossenen kontinuierlichen Gruppe, Math. Ann. 97 (1927)
H. Weyl, Gruppentheorie und Quantenmechanik (1928)
E. Wigner, Gruppentheorie und ihre Anwendung auf die Quantenmechanik der Atomspektren (1931)
secondary: G. W. Mackey, Harmonic analysis as the exploitation of symmetry - a historical survey, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.) 3 (1980)

events.name: Ergodic theory from statistical mechanics
events.datesNote: Boltzmann's ergodic hypothesis (1870s); Koopman's Hilbert-space formulation (1931), von Neumann's mean (1932) and Birkhoff's pointwise (1931) theorems.
events.summary: The ergodic hypothesis of statistical mechanics is turned into a theorem about measure-preserving transformations, using Hilbert-space and measure-theoretic tools.
keyWorks: B. O. Koopman, Hamiltonian systems and transformations in Hilbert space, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 17 (1931)
G. D. Birkhoff, Proof of the ergodic theorem, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 17 (1931)
J. von Neumann, Proof of the quasi-ergodic hypothesis, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 18 (1932)
secondary: G. W. Mackey, Ergodic theory and its significance for statistical mechanics and probability theory, Adv. Math. 12 (1974)

events.name: Computability theory
events.datesNote: Godel (1931), Church and Turing (1936); Post (1944) and Kleene's work consolidate recursion theory.
events.summary: Hilbert's decision problem and the incompleteness phenomenon are answered by a precise notion of effective procedure, which becomes an object of study.
keyWorks: K. Godel, Uber formal unentscheidbare Satze der Principia Mathematica und verwandter Systeme I, Monatsh. Math. Phys. 38 (1931)
A. Church, An unsolvable problem of elementary number theory, Amer. J. Math. 58 (1936)
A. M. Turing, On computable numbers, with an application to the Entscheidungsproblem, Proc. London Math. Soc. (2) 42 (1936)
secondary: R. I. Soare, Computability and recursion, Bull. Symbolic Logic 2 (1996)
M. Davis, The Universal Computer: The Road from Leibniz to Turing (2000)

events.name: Weil's dictionary: number fields, function fields, Riemann surfaces
events.datesNote: Dedekind-Weber (1882) set up the analogy for function fields; Weil states it as a three-column table in a 1940 letter and then uses it in the Weil conjectures programme.
events.summary: A three-way analogy between number fields, function fields over finite fields and compact Riemann surfaces transfers statements and methods between arithmetic and geometry.
keyWorks: R. Dedekind and H. Weber, Theorie der algebraischen Functionen einer Veranderlichen, J. reine angew. Math. 92 (1882)
A. Weil, letter to Simone Weil (March 1940, written from Bonne-Nouvelle prison, Rouen), in Oeuvres scientifiques / Collected Papers, vol. I (1979)
secondary: M. H. Krieger, translation of Weil's 1940 letter, Notices Amer. Math. Soc. 52 (2005) 334-341
M. H. Krieger, Doing Mathematics: Convention, Subject, Calculation, Analogy (2003), Appendix D

events.name: Information theory
events.datesNote: Shannon's paper (1948); IRE Professional Group on Information Theory formed 1951, its Transactions began 1953 and became IRE Transactions on Information Theory in 1955.
events.summary: Communication-engineering questions are given a probabilistic theory with entropy as the central quantity and coding theorems as results.
keyWorks: C. E. Shannon, A mathematical theory of communication, Bell System Tech. J. 27 (1948)
secondary: S. Verdu, Fifty years of Shannon theory, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 44 (1998)
J. Soni and R. Goodman, A Mind at Play (2017)

events.name: Game theory
events.datesNote: Minimax theorem (1928), Theory of Games and Economic Behavior (1944), Nash equilibrium (1950).
events.summary: Strategic interaction is given a mathematical model, with minimax and equilibrium existence proved by convexity and fixed-point arguments.
keyWorks: J. von Neumann, Zur Theorie der Gesellschaftsspiele, Math. Ann. 100 (1928)
J. von Neumann and O. Morgenstern, Theory of Games and Economic Behavior (1944)
J. F. Nash, Equilibrium points in n-person games, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 36 (1950)
secondary: R. J. Leonard, Von Neumann, Morgenstern, and the Creation of Game Theory (2010)

events.name: The probabilistic method in combinatorics
events.datesNote: Erdos's Ramsey lower bound (1947), random graphs (1959-60); Alon-Spencer text (1992).
events.summary: Existence of a combinatorial object is proved by showing a random object has the property with positive probability.
keyWorks: P. Erdos, Some remarks on the theory of graphs, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 53 (1947)
P. Erdos and A. Renyi, On random graphs I, Publ. Math. Debrecen 6 (1959)
N. Alon and J. Spencer, The Probabilistic Method (1992)
secondary: J. Spencer, Ten Lectures on the Probabilistic Method (1994)

events.name: Category theory and homological algebra
events.datesNote: Eilenberg-Mac Lane (1945); Cartan-Eilenberg (1956) and Grothendieck's Tohoku paper (1957).
events.summary: Natural isomorphisms noticed in homology computations are formalised as functors and natural transformations, and the resulting structure becomes a general language.
keyWorks: S. Eilenberg and S. Mac Lane, General theory of natural equivalences, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 58 (1945)
H. Cartan and S. Eilenberg, Homological Algebra (1956)
A. Grothendieck, Sur quelques points d'algebre homologique, Tohoku Math. J. (2) 9 (1957)
secondary: R. Kromer, Tool and Object: A History and Philosophy of Category Theory (2007)
C. A. Weibel, History of homological algebra, in I. M. James (ed.), History of Topology (1999)

events.name: Fourier analysis for density problems (Roth)
events.datesNote: Roth (1953) for length-3 progressions; Gowers (1998-2001) extends the method to all lengths via higher-order uniformity.
events.summary: A circle-method style Fourier argument with a density-increment iteration shows dense integer sets contain three-term progressions.
keyWorks: K. F. Roth, On certain sets of integers, J. London Math. Soc. 28 (1953)
W. T. Gowers, A new proof of Szemeredi's theorem, Geom. Funct. Anal. 11 (2001)
secondary: T. Tao, The ergodic and combinatorial approaches to Szemeredi's theorem, in Additive Combinatorics, CRM Proc. Lecture Notes 43 (2007)

events.name: Sheaf theory
events.datesNote: Leray's work (1945, in captivity), Cartan seminars (1948-54), Serre's FAC (1955).
events.summary: Local-to-global problems from topology and several complex variables are packaged as sheaves with cohomology, then moved into algebraic geometry.
keyWorks: J. Leray, Sur la forme des espaces topologiques et sur les points fixes des representations, J. Math. Pures Appl. 24 (1945)
J.-P. Serre, Faisceaux algebriques coherents, Ann. of Math. 61 (1955)
secondary: J. W. Gray, Fragments of the history of sheaf theory, in Applications of Sheaves, Lecture Notes in Math. 753 (1979)

events.name: Scheme theory
events.datesNote: Grothendieck's ICM 1958 talk, then EGA (1960-67) and SGA seminars.
events.summary: Algebraic geometry is rebuilt on arbitrary commutative rings so that geometry over the integers and over finite fields is treated uniformly with complex varieties.
keyWorks: A. Grothendieck, The cohomology theory of abstract algebraic varieties, Proc. ICM Edinburgh (1958)
A. Grothendieck and J. Dieudonne, Elements de geometrie algebrique I-IV, Publ. Math. IHES 4, 8, 11, 17, 20, 24, 28, 32 (1960-67)
secondary: J. Dieudonne, The historical development of algebraic geometry, Amer. Math. Monthly 79 (1972)
P. Cartier, A mad day's work: from Grothendieck to Connes and Kontsevich, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 38 (2001)

events.name: Weil conjectures: topology enters arithmetic
events.datesNote: Weil's 1949 conjectures; Dwork's rationality (1960), Grothendieck's etale cohomology (1960s), Deligne's proof of the Riemann hypothesis part (1974).
events.summary: Counting points on varieties over finite fields is predicted to behave like Betti numbers, and a cohomology theory built for that purpose proves it.
keyWorks: A. Weil, Numbers of solutions of equations in finite fields, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 55 (1949)
B. Dwork, On the rationality of the zeta function of an algebraic variety, Amer. J. Math. 82 (1960)
P. Deligne, La conjecture de Weil. I, Publ. Math. IHES 43 (1974)
secondary: N. M. Katz, An overview of Deligne's proof of the Riemann hypothesis for varieties over finite fields, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 28 (1976)

events.name: Logic solves Hilbert's tenth problem
events.datesNote: Davis-Putnam-Robinson (1961) reduce to a statement about exponential growth; Matiyasevich (1970) supplies it.
events.summary: Recursively enumerable sets are shown to be Diophantine, so no algorithm decides solvability of Diophantine equations.
keyWorks: M. Davis, H. Putnam and J. Robinson, The decision problem for exponential Diophantine equations, Ann. of Math. 74 (1961)
Yu. V. Matiyasevich, Enumerable sets are Diophantine, Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 191 (1970)
secondary: M. Davis, Hilbert's tenth problem is unsolvable, Amer. Math. Monthly 80 (1973)
Yu. V. Matiyasevich, Hilbert's Tenth Problem (1993)

events.name: Atiyah-Singer index theorem and K-theory
events.datesNote: Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch (1957, Borel-Serre 1958), Atiyah-Hirzebruch K-theory (1959-61), index theorem announced 1963, proved 1968.
events.summary: The analytic index of an elliptic operator is computed from topological data via K-theory, connecting PDE, characteristic classes and algebraic geometry.
keyWorks: A. Borel and J.-P. Serre, Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch, Bull. Soc. Math. France 86 (1958)
M. F. Atiyah and F. Hirzebruch, Vector bundles and homogeneous spaces, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 3 (1961)
M. F. Atiyah and I. M. Singer, The index of elliptic operators on compact manifolds, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 69 (1963)
M. F. Atiyah and I. M. Singer, The index of elliptic operators I, Ann. of Math. 87 (1968)
secondary: J. Dieudonne, A History of Algebraic and Differential Topology, 1900-1960 (1989)

events.name: The Langlands programme
events.datesNote: Precursors: Hecke, Tate's thesis (1950), Weil's dictionary; Langlands letter to Weil (1967) and 1970 lectures.
events.summary: Galois representations are conjecturally matched with automorphic representations, linking arithmetic, representation theory and harmonic analysis.
keyWorks: R. P. Langlands, letter to A. Weil (January 1967)
R. P. Langlands, Problems in the theory of automorphic forms, in Lectures in Modern Analysis and Applications III, Lecture Notes in Math. 170 (1970)
J. Tate, Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions (1950; in Cassels-Frohlich, Algebraic Number Theory, 1967)
secondary: S. Gelbart, An elementary introduction to the Langlands program, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 10 (1984)
E. Frenkel, Love and Math (2013)

events.name: Unipotent flows and the Oppenheim conjecture
events.datesNote: Margulis (1987) proves Oppenheim via dynamics on SL(3,R)/SL(3,Z); Ratner's theorems (1991) generalise.
events.summary: Values of indefinite quadratic forms at integer points are controlled by showing orbits of unipotent subgroups on homogeneous spaces are well-behaved.
keyWorks: G. A. Margulis, Indefinite quadratic forms and unipotent flows on homogeneous spaces, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Ser. I 304 (1987)
M. Ratner, On Raghunathan's measure conjecture, Ann. of Math. 134 (1991)
secondary: G. A. Margulis, Oppenheim conjecture, in Fields Medallists' Lectures (1997)
D. W. Morris, Ratner's Theorems on Unipotent Flows (2005)

events.name: Topology proves Kneser's conjecture
events.datesNote: Lovasz (1978) with Barany's short proof; Matousek's book (2003) consolidates the area.
events.summary: The chromatic number of Kneser graphs is bounded below via the Borsuk-Ulam theorem applied to a topological space built from the graph.
keyWorks: L. Lovasz, Kneser's conjecture, chromatic number, and homotopy, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 25 (1978)
I. Barany, A short proof of Kneser's conjecture, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 25 (1978)
secondary: J. Matousek, Using the Borsuk-Ulam Theorem (2003)

events.name: Random matrix statistics and the zeros of zeta
events.datesNote: Montgomery's pair correlation (1973), Odlyzko's numerics (1987), Katz-Sarnak for function fields (1999).
events.summary: The pair correlation of zeta zeros matches that of eigenvalues of random unitary matrices, suggesting a spectral interpretation of the zeros.
keyWorks: H. L. Montgomery, The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 24 (1973)
A. M. Odlyzko, On the distribution of spacings between zeros of the zeta function, Math. Comp. 48 (1987)
N. M. Katz and P. Sarnak, Random Matrices, Frobenius Eigenvalues, and Monodromy (1999)
secondary: Z. Rudnick and P. Sarnak, Zeros of principal L-functions and random matrix theory, Duke Math. J. 81 (1996)
J. B. Conrey, The Riemann hypothesis, Notices Amer. Math. Soc. 50 (2003)

events.name: Furstenberg: ergodic theory proves Szemeredi's theorem
events.datesNote: Szemeredi (1975, combinatorial); Furstenberg (1977) via multiple recurrence; Furstenberg's 1981 book.
events.summary: Density statements about integers are translated into recurrence statements for measure-preserving systems and proved there.
keyWorks: E. Szemeredi, On sets of integers containing no k elements in arithmetic progression, Acta Arith. 27 (1975)
H. Furstenberg, Ergodic behavior of diagonal measures and a theorem of Szemeredi on arithmetic progressions, J. Analyse Math. 31 (1977)
H. Furstenberg, Recurrence in Ergodic Theory and Combinatorial Number Theory (1981)
secondary: T. Tao, The ergodic and combinatorial approaches to Szemeredi's theorem, in Additive Combinatorics, CRM Proc. Lecture Notes 43 (2007)

events.name: Geometric group theory
events.datesNote: Gromov's polynomial growth theorem (1981) and hyperbolic groups (1987); the 1993 Sussex symposium volume names the field.
events.summary: Finitely generated groups are studied as metric spaces up to quasi-isometry, so large-scale geometry classifies algebraic properties.
keyWorks: M. Gromov, Groups of polynomial growth and expanding maps, Publ. Math. IHES 53 (1981)
M. Gromov, Hyperbolic groups, in Essays in Group Theory, MSRI Publ. 8 (1987)
secondary: M. R. Bridson and A. Haefliger, Metric Spaces of Non-Positive Curvature (1999)
P. de la Harpe, Topics in Geometric Group Theory (2000)

events.name: Noncommutative geometry
events.datesNote: Connes (1980-85); the 1994 book consolidates.
events.summary: Geometric invariants (cohomology, index theory) are extended to operator algebras viewed as spaces of noncommutative functions.
keyWorks: A. Connes, Non-commutative differential geometry, Publ. Math. IHES 62 (1985)
A. Connes, Noncommutative Geometry (1994)
secondary: P. Cartier, A mad day's work: from Grothendieck to Connes and Kontsevich, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 38 (2001)

events.name: Gauge theory transforms four-manifold topology
events.datesNote: Donaldson (1983) with Yang-Mills moduli spaces; Seiberg-Witten equations (1994) from supersymmetric field theory; Donaldson-Kronheimer (1990).
events.summary: Solutions of the Yang-Mills and later Seiberg-Witten equations give invariants distinguishing smooth structures on four-manifolds, results unreachable by classical topology.
keyWorks: S. K. Donaldson, An application of gauge theory to four-dimensional topology, J. Differential Geom. 18 (1983)
M. H. Freedman, The topology of four-dimensional manifolds, J. Differential Geom. 17 (1982)
E. Witten, Monopoles and four-manifolds, Math. Res. Lett. 1 (1994)
secondary: S. K. Donaldson and P. B. Kronheimer, The Geometry of Four-Manifolds (1990)

events.name: Jones polynomial from operator algebras
events.datesNote: Jones (1985) from subfactor theory; Witten's Chern-Simons interpretation (1989).
events.summary: A representation of the braid groups arising from von Neumann algebras yields a new knot invariant, later interpreted through quantum field theory.
keyWorks: V. F. R. Jones, A polynomial invariant for knots via von Neumann algebras, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.) 12 (1985)
V. F. R. Jones, Hecke algebra representations of braid groups and link polynomials, Ann. of Math. 126 (1987)
E. Witten, Quantum field theory and the Jones polynomial, Comm. Math. Phys. 121 (1989)
secondary: V. F. R. Jones, Subfactors and Knots, CBMS Regional Conf. Ser. in Math. 80 (1991)

events.name: Symplectic topology
events.datesNote: Hamiltonian mechanics and Arnold's conjectures (1960s-1974); Gromov's pseudoholomorphic curves (1985); Floer homology (1988); McDuff-Salamon (1995).
events.summary: The geometry of phase space is studied by rigidity phenomena, using complex-geometric techniques (holomorphic curves) and Morse-theoretic ones (Floer homology).
keyWorks: V. I. Arnold, Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics (Russian 1974; English 1978)
M. Gromov, Pseudo holomorphic curves in symplectic manifolds, Invent. Math. 82 (1985)
A. Floer, Morse theory for Lagrangian intersections, J. Differential Geom. 28 (1988)
secondary: D. McDuff and D. Salamon, Introduction to Symplectic Topology (1995)
D. McDuff, Symplectic structures - a new approach to geometry, Notices Amer. Math. Soc. 45 (1998)

events.name: Monstrous moonshine
events.datesNote: McKay's observation (1978) and the Conway-Norton conjectures (1979); vertex operator construction (1988); Borcherds's proof (1992).
events.summary: Dimensions of representations of the Monster group match coefficients of the modular function j, and a proof requires a new algebraic structure from string theory.
keyWorks: J. H. Conway and S. P. Norton, Monstrous moonshine, Bull. London Math. Soc. 11 (1979)
I. Frenkel, J. Lepowsky and A. Meurman, Vertex Operator Algebras and the Monster (1988)
R. E. Borcherds, Monstrous moonshine and monstrous Lie superalgebras, Invent. Math. 109 (1992)
secondary: T. Gannon, Moonshine beyond the Monster (2006)
M. Ronan, Symmetry and the Monster (2006)

events.name: Two-dimensional gravity and the moduli space of curves
events.datesNote: Witten's conjecture (1991), Kontsevich's proof via ribbon graphs (1992), Mirzakhani's independent proof via hyperbolic volumes (2007).
events.summary: A prediction of topological gravity about intersection numbers on moduli spaces of curves is proved by combinatorial (ribbon graph) and hyperbolic-geometric routes.
keyWorks: E. Witten, Two-dimensional gravity and intersection theory on moduli space, Surveys in Differential Geometry 1 (1991)
M. Kontsevich, Intersection theory on the moduli space of curves and the matrix Airy function, Comm. Math. Phys. 147 (1992)
M. Mirzakhani, Weil-Petersson volumes and intersection theory on the moduli space of curves, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 20 (2007)

events.name: Model theory in diophantine geometry
events.datesNote: Hrushovski (1996) via stability theory; Pila-Wilkie (2006) and Pila (2011) via o-minimality.
events.summary: Stability and o-minimality results from model theory prove the Mordell-Lang conjecture for function fields and cases of Andre-Oort.
keyWorks: E. Hrushovski, The Mordell-Lang conjecture for function fields, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 9 (1996)
J. Pila and A. J. Wilkie, The rational points of a definable set, Duke Math. J. 133 (2006)
J. Pila, O-minimality and the Andre-Oort conjecture for C^n, Ann. of Math. 173 (2011)
secondary: E. Bouscaren (ed.), Model Theory and Algebraic Geometry: An Introduction to E. Hrushovski's Proof of the Geometric Mordell-Lang Conjecture, Lecture Notes in Math. 1696 (1998)

events.name: Mirror symmetry
events.datesNote: Candelas et al. (1991) predict counts of rational curves; Kontsevich's homological mirror symmetry (1994); Givental's proof (1996-98); Cox-Katz (1999).
events.summary: A duality between Calabi-Yau manifolds from string theory predicts numbers of rational curves, later proved mathematically and recast as an equivalence of categories.
keyWorks: P. Candelas, X. de la Ossa, P. Green and L. Parkes, A pair of Calabi-Yau manifolds as an exactly soluble superconformal theory, Nucl. Phys. B 359 (1991)
M. Kontsevich, Homological algebra of mirror symmetry, Proc. ICM Zurich 1994, vol. 1 (1995)
A. Givental, Equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants, Internat. Math. Res. Notices (1996)
secondary: D. A. Cox and S. Katz, Mirror Symmetry and Algebraic Geometry (1999)
K. Hori et al., Mirror Symmetry (Clay Mathematics Monographs, 2003)

events.name: Modularity of elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem
events.datesNote: Taniyama-Shimura conjecture (1955-57); Frey (1986) and Ribet (1990) link it to Fermat; Wiles and Taylor-Wiles (1995).
events.summary: A counterexample to Fermat would give an elliptic curve contradicting modularity, and modularity of semistable curves is proved with Galois deformation theory and Hecke algebras.
keyWorks: G. Frey, Links between stable elliptic curves and certain Diophantine equations, Ann. Univ. Sarav. Ser. Math. 1 (1986)
K. A. Ribet, On modular representations of Gal(Q-bar/Q) arising from modular forms, Invent. Math. 100 (1990)
A. Wiles, Modular elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem, Ann. of Math. 141 (1995)
R. Taylor and A. Wiles, Ring-theoretic properties of certain Hecke algebras, Ann. of Math. 141 (1995)
secondary: G. Cornell, J. H. Silverman and G. Stevens (eds.), Modular Forms and Fermat's Last Theorem (1997)

events.name: Schramm-Loewner evolution
events.datesNote: Schramm (2000); Lawler-Schramm-Werner (2004); Smirnov's Ising proof (2010); Lawler's book (2005).
events.summary: Scaling limits of planar lattice models are described by random curves generated by Loewner's equation driven by Brownian motion, giving rigorous access to conformal field theory predictions.
keyWorks: O. Schramm, Scaling limits of loop-erased random walks and uniform spanning trees, Israel J. Math. 118 (2000)
G. F. Lawler, O. Schramm and W. Werner, Conformal invariance of planar loop-erased random walks and uniform spanning trees, Ann. Probab. 32 (2004)
S. Smirnov, Conformal invariance in random cluster models. I. Holomorphic fermions in the Ising model, Ann. of Math. 172 (2010)
secondary: G. F. Lawler, Conformally Invariant Processes in the Plane (2005)
W. Werner, Random planar curves and Schramm-Loewner evolutions, Lecture Notes in Math. 1840 (2004)

events.name: Green-Tao: primes contain long arithmetic progressions
events.datesNote: Preprint 2004; Annals 2008.
events.summary: Szemeredi's theorem is extended to a pseudorandom majorant via a transference principle, with sieve-theoretic input showing the primes sit inside one, using Gowers norms and ergodic-style structure theory.
keyWorks: B. Green and T. Tao, The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions, Ann. of Math. 167 (2008)
secondary: T. Tao, The dichotomy between structure and randomness, arithmetic progressions, and the primes, Proc. ICM Madrid 2006, vol. 1 (2007)
B. Kra, The Green-Tao theorem on arithmetic progressions in the primes: an ergodic point of view, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 43 (2006)

events.name: The polynomial method in combinatorics
events.datesNote: Dvir (2008, publ. 2009); Guth-Katz (2010, publ. 2015); Guth's book (2016).
events.summary: Low-degree polynomials vanishing on a point set give short proofs of the finite-field Kakeya problem and the Erdos distinct-distances problem in the plane.
keyWorks: Z. Dvir, On the size of Kakeya sets in finite fields, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 22 (2009)
L. Guth and N. H. Katz, On the Erdos distinct distances problem in the plane, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015)
secondary: L. Guth, Polynomial Methods in Combinatorics (2016)

events.name: Additive combinatorics proves expansion in groups
events.datesNote: Bourgain-Katz-Tao sum-product in finite fields (2004); Helfgott (2008) and Bourgain-Gamburd (2008).
events.summary: Sum-product and product-set growth estimates show that Cayley graphs of SL2(Fp) are expanders, a spectral gap statement about groups.
keyWorks: J. Bourgain, N. Katz and T. Tao, A sum-product estimate in finite fields, and applications, Geom. Funct. Anal. 14 (2004)
H. A. Helfgott, Growth and generation in SL2(Z/pZ), Ann. of Math. 167 (2008)
J. Bourgain and A. Gamburd, Uniform expansion bounds for Cayley graphs of SL2(Fp), Ann. of Math. 167 (2008)
secondary: A. Lubotzky, Expander graphs in pure and applied mathematics, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 49 (2012)
T. Tao, Expansion in Finite Simple Groups of Lie Type (2015)

events.name: Perelman's proof of the Poincare conjecture
events.datesNote: Hamilton's Ricci flow (1982); Perelman's three preprints (2002-03).
events.summary: Ricci flow with surgery, controlled by an entropy functional and Alexandrov-space compactness, classifies three-manifolds and gives the Poincare and geometrisation conjectures.
keyWorks: R. S. Hamilton, Three-manifolds with positive Ricci curvature, J. Differential Geom. 17 (1982)
G. Perelman, The entropy formula for the Ricci flow and its geometric applications, arXiv:math/0211159 (2002)
G. Perelman, Ricci flow with surgery on three-manifolds, arXiv:math/0303109 (2003)
G. Perelman, Finite extinction time for the solutions to the Ricci flow on certain three-manifolds, arXiv:math/0307245 (2003)
secondary: J. Morgan and G. Tian, Ricci Flow and the Poincare Conjecture (2007)
B. Kleiner and J. Lott, Notes on Perelman's papers, Geom. Topol. 12 (2008)

events.name: Sphere packing in dimensions 8 and 24
events.datesNote: Cohn-Elkies linear programming bound (2003); Viazovska (2016, publ. 2017).
events.summary: A modular-form construction produces the magic function required by the Fourier linear programming bound, matching the E8 and Leech lattice packing densities.
keyWorks: H. Cohn and N. Elkies, New upper bounds on sphere packings I, Ann. of Math. 157 (2003)
M. S. Viazovska, The sphere packing problem in dimension 8, Ann. of Math. 185 (2017)
H. Cohn, A. Kumar, S. D. Miller, D. Radchenko and M. Viazovska, The sphere packing problem in dimension 24, Ann. of Math. 185 (2017)
secondary: H. Cohn, A conceptual breakthrough in sphere packing, Notices Amer. Math. Soc. 64 (2017)

events.name: Optimal transport and synthetic Ricci curvature
events.product: Metric-measure geometry with Ricci curvature bounds
events.datesNote: Sturm (2006) and Lott-Villani (2009); Villani's book (2009).
events.summary: Lower Ricci curvature bounds are defined on non-smooth spaces by convexity of entropy along optimal transport geodesics, giving a stable notion under Gromov-Hausdorff limits.
keyWorks: Y. Brenier, Polar factorization and monotone rearrangement of vector-valued functions, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 44 (1991)
K.-T. Sturm, On the geometry of metric measure spaces. I, II, Acta Math. 196 (2006)
J. Lott and C. Villani, Ricci curvature for metric-measure spaces via optimal transport, Ann. of Math. 169 (2009)
secondary: C. Villani, Optimal Transport: Old and New (2009)

events.name: Hodge theory proves log-concavity conjectures
events.datesNote: Huh (2012) for graphs; Adiprasito-Huh-Katz (2018) for matroids.
events.summary: Heron-Rota-Welsh log-concavity of chromatic polynomials and Rota's conjecture are proved using Hodge-Riemann relations on Chow rings of matroid-like objects.
keyWorks: J. Huh, Milnor numbers of projective hypersurfaces and the chromatic polynomial of a graph, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 25 (2012)
J. Huh and E. Katz, Log-concavity of characteristic polynomials and the Bergman fan of matroids, Math. Ann. 354 (2012)
K. Adiprasito, J. Huh and E. Katz, Hodge theory for combinatorial geometries, Ann. of Math. 188 (2018)
secondary: E. Katz, Matroid theory for algebraic geometers, in Nonarchimedean and Tropical Geometry (2016)

events.name: Regularity structures
events.product: Regularity structures; singular stochastic PDE theory
events.datesNote: Lyons's rough paths (1998), Connes-Kreimer's Hopf algebra of renormalisation (1998), Hairer's theory (2014), algebraic renormalisation (2019).
events.summary: Ill-posed stochastic PDEs are solved by combining rough-path ideas with a Hopf-algebraic account of renormalisation taken from quantum field theory.
keyWorks: T. J. Lyons, Differential equations driven by rough signals, Rev. Mat. Iberoamericana 14 (1998)
A. Connes and D. Kreimer, Hopf algebras, renormalization and noncommutative geometry, Comm. Math. Phys. 199 (1998)
M. Hairer, A theory of regularity structures, Invent. Math. 198 (2014)
Y. Bruned, M. Hairer and L. Zambotti, Algebraic renormalisation of regularity structures, Invent. Math. 215 (2019)
secondary: P. K. Friz and M. Hairer, A Course on Rough Paths (2nd ed., 2020)

events.name: Erdos discrepancy problem
events.datesNote: Problem posed in 1932; Polymath5 (2010) reduces it to multiplicative functions; Tao (2015) closes it with a logarithmically averaged Elliott-type theorem built on Matomaki-Radziwill.
events.summary: A combinatorial discrepancy question is reduced to correlations of multiplicative functions, then settled with entropy-decrement and short-interval results from analytic number theory.
keyWorks: T. Tao, The logarithmically averaged Chowla and Elliott conjectures for two-point correlations, Forum Math. Pi 4 (2016)
T. Tao, The Erdos discrepancy problem, Discrete Anal. 2016:1
K. Matomaki and M. Radziwill, Multiplicative functions in short intervals, Ann. of Math. 183 (2016)
secondary: B. Konev and A. Lisitsa, Computer-aided proof of Erdos discrepancy properties, Artificial Intelligence 224 (2015)
Polymath5 project, Erdos discrepancy problem (2010)

events.name: Entropy proves the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture
events.datesNote: Entropy methods in additive combinatorics from Ruzsa and Tao in the 2000s; GGMT proof of Marton's conjecture in 2023; Lean formalisation in the same period.
events.summary: Entropy of random variables, rather than sets, is used with a doubling-style argument to settle the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture in characteristic 2.
keyWorks: W. T. Gowers, B. Green, F. Manners and T. Tao, On a conjecture of Marton, arXiv:2311.05762 (2023)
secondary: T. Tao, Formalizing the proof of PFR in Lean4 using Blueprint: a short tour (blog post, 18 November 2023)
PFR formalisation project (github.com/teorth/pfr; blueprint at teorth.github.io/pfr); reported complete in about three weeks

events.name: Computer science separates from mathematics
events.datesNote: First university departments in the 1960s (Purdue, October 1962, confirmed; Stanford 1965 from a single source); the field's relation to mathematics remains contested.
events.summary: Computability, switching theory and programming grow into a discipline with its own departments, journals and questions (complexity, algorithms) while keeping heavy mathematical exchange.
keyWorks: A. M. Turing, On computable numbers (1936)
D. E. Knuth, Computer science and its relation to mathematics, Amer. Math. Monthly 81 (1974)
secondary: M. Tedre, The Science of Computing: Shaping a Discipline (2014)
P. J. Denning et al., Computing as a discipline, Commun. ACM 32 (1989)
